text: After two dates, they have already planned your summer together. You have not agreed to a third date yet.
discussion: Cute enthusiasm or a lot to sign up for?

text: They book a surprise date, but first ask about your budget, food allergies, and when you need to be home.
discussion: Do you like a surprise or want the full itinerary?

text: They never post you, but their friends and family all know you are together.
discussion: Does it count if it is not on Instagram?

text: They keep your relationship off social media and ask you to pretend you are just friends when someone flirts with them.
discussion: Where does privacy become secrecy?

text: They are close friends with an ex. You have met them, and nobody acts weird about it.
discussion: Could you actually be relaxed about this?

text: Every ex is apparently crazy. Somehow, they have never been the problem.
discussion: Bad luck or a suspiciously consistent story?

text: They take hours to reply at work, then call you in the evening and remember everything you told them.
discussion: How long is too long to wait for a text?

text: They disappear for a week, then come back with a perfect date and a very convincing smile. It keeps happening.
discussion: Be honest. How many times would the smile work?

text: They say they are not looking for anything serious. You are, but the chemistry is ridiculous.
discussion: They have been honest. Would you believe them or stay and hope?

text: They call you their soulmate in private but avoid the question every time you ask whether you are exclusive.
discussion: How long would you let this stay undefined?

text: They admit they felt jealous, ask for a little reassurance, and still tell you to enjoy your night out.
discussion: Is a little jealousy flattering?

text: They say they just miss you, then get cold with you whenever you make plans without them.
discussion: Would you find yourself cancelling plans?

text: They insist on paying for dinner, then say you owe them another date because it was expensive.
discussion: Would you ask for the bill back?

text: They suggest splitting the first date bill. They also planned the date and travelled an hour to meet you.
discussion: Does splitting the bill change the vibe?

text: They have a spreadsheet for their budget and suggest a picnic because dinner out is not in it this week.
discussion: Responsible or a romance killer?

text: They buy you expensive gifts, then bring up the price whenever you disagree with them.
discussion: At what point would you hand the gift back?

text: They remember tiny things you mention and bring your favourite snack on a day you are stressed.
discussion: What small gesture would win you over immediately?

text: They turn up at your place with flowers after you have said you want the evening to yourself.
discussion: Would the flowers make you change your mind?

text: They ask to pause an argument until tomorrow morning, then actually bring it up over breakfast.
discussion: Could you sleep before sorting it out?

text: After an argument, they act extra affectionate but say talking about what happened would ruin the mood.
discussion: Would you let it go if the rest of the night was lovely?

text: They are kind and consistent. Your friends love them. You are wondering whether things feel a little too calm.
discussion: Bored, or just not used to calm?

text: They keep joking about dating your friend. When you say it bothers you, they tell the joke again.
discussion: Does being funny buy anyone extra chances?

text: They ask what you like instead of trying to act as though they already know everything about romance.
discussion: Do you like being asked, or want them to just know?

text: They choose your meal for you every time, even after you have said you want to order for yourself.
discussion: When does taking charge stop being attractive?

text: They are still on a dating app after you both agreed to be exclusive. They say they only like the attention.
discussion: Would the explanation make any difference?

text: Their best friend is someone they could be attracted to. They include you in plans and are open about the friendship.
discussion: Would you trust it, or keep an eye on things?

text: They check their phone under the table whenever you talk, then say you are their favourite person to spend time with.
discussion: How much does phone etiquette matter on a date?

text: They put their phone on silent during dates but keep one contact able to ring through because they care for a parent.
discussion: What interruptions are fair game?

text: They keep making little comments about your clothes, then offer to buy outfits they would prefer you to wear.
discussion: A style suggestion or a whole new wardrobe of problems?

text: They love a hobby you find painfully boring. They do not expect you to join in and make time for your plans too.
discussion: Which hobby would still give you the ick?

text: They cancel again, but send a voice note so charming that you are smiling before it ends. They do not suggest another day.
discussion: Can good flirting carry bad planning?

text: They are awkward at flirting but always follow through on plans. Their texts read like work emails.
discussion: Would you give a bad texter a chance?
